{
  "hypothesis": "Predicted that individuals with PTSD would exhibit impaired inhibitory control over memory retrieval compared to trauma-exposed control participants, resulting in reduced suppression-induced forgetting of aversive scenes.",
  "design": "mixed, with group (PTSD, control) as a between-subjects factor and condition (baseline, suppress) as a within-subjects factor.",
  "manipulation_or_predictor": "The Think/No-Think (TNT) task, where participants were instructed to either recall (think) or suppress (no-think) memories for previously studied aversive object-scene pairs.",
  "outcome_measure": "Memory performance for scenes (identification, gist, and details) measured at a final test phase, specifically comparing performance between suppress and baseline conditions.",
  "population_and_setting": "18 individuals with a current diagnosis of PTSD and 18 trauma-exposed control individuals recruited from the local community and departmental participant panels.",
  "sample_size_total": 36,
  "recruitment_and_incentive": "Recruited through print advertisements; no specific incentive mentioned.",
  "analysis_plan": "Mixed analysis of variance (ANOVA) with condition (baseline, suppress) as a within-subjects factor and group (PTSD, control) as a between-subjects factor, performed separately for each dependent measure.",
  "preregistered_or_confirmatory": "not stated",
  "other_methods_notes": "Participants were matched on time since trauma. Exclusion criteria included psychosis or borderline personality disorder for PTSD group, and any current psychiatric disorder for control group. Stimuli were 60 object-scene pairs (48 critical, 12 fillers). Suppression-induced forgetting was defined as lower memory performance for suppress items compared with baseline items."
}
